description: A melody generator after the CGS Infinite Melody: one bit shift register feeding four analogue shift registers, whose bits are weighted and summed into voltages

params.text: Scales the voltage leaving that stage's output
Sets the level the incoming signal is compared against: the comparator reads a one above it and a zero below
Chooses how an ADVANCE pulse fills the four shift registers: either the contents shift along the chain a register per pulse, or the second, third and fourth take theirs every two, four and eight
Chooses between a major and a minor scale
Switches that bit of the register on and off
How much that bit of the register contributes to the summed output
Sets the base voltage the melody is built on, in octaves
Sets the voltage between one step of the melody and the next

inputs.text: A voltage setting the spacing between one step of the melody and the next
A voltage sets the level the incoming signal is compared against, in place of the SENSE knob
The signal the bits are read from. A lamp lights while the signal is above the comparison level, which is the one written into the register at the next clock
A voltage setting the base the melody is built on, at 1V per octave
A voltage chooses the way an ADVANCE pulse fills the four shift registers, in place of the MODE switch
A gate chooses between a major and a minor scale
A pulse moves the bit register's contents on into the four shift registers, in the way MODE sets
A pulse shifts the bit register one place along and writes the comparator's current state into the first bit
A gate switches that bit of the register on and off

outputs.text: A melody voltage from one of the module's three stages, at the level set by that stage's trimmer
The melody voltage quantised to a diatonic scale
The six bits of the register summed at the weights set in the bit mixer

notes: a signal has to be patched to the noise input and a clock to the clock input before any melody appears
the clock writes one bit into the register each pulse: a one while the signal is above the SENSE level, a zero while it is below
the four shift registers are filled only by pulses at the ADVANCE input, which is a second clock separate from the one that fills the bit register.

inputs.3: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
